text.p: Texas Instruments Inc has taken a broad license for Rambus Inc's high-bandwidth memory-interface technology, the companies said Monday.

TI will use the technology in several next-generation products, including digital signal processors (DSPs) and dynamic random access memories (DRAMs). Initial products using the technology are scheduled to sample early in 1998, the companies said.

"On the memory side, TI plans to use the Direct Rambus interface in the company's 64-megabit and higher density DRAM devices. The Direct Rambus interface is designed to support the higher bandwidth applications that will be required to keep up with the increased processor and logic performances of the future," said Ramesh Gidwani, Texas Instruments's memory vice president.
Rambus's stock gained 4-1/4 to 49. TI's stock added 11/16 to 64-1/2.
